pages.text: "The ice boat!" Bung pointed ahead. Grandpa lifted his oar. Their boat stopped in the waterway. Two boats ahead, theirs last.
"A block for Mom!" Bung tugged Grandpa's arm. "Forward, quickly!" Ddori watched the ice boat beside Bung.
Bung stamped the board, rocking the stopped boat. Ddori landed on the bottom. "Ah!" Grandpa put down the oar to sit Ddori up.
The boats ahead moved, but theirs stayed. An empty space! A boat from behind slipped into it.
"Even farther back now!" Bung pouted. White ice kept dwindling. Bung stopped stamping and sat on the board.
Grandpa watched. "If you sold ice, would you want to give it to a boat that cut in?" Bung shook the head.
The next boat moved. Grandpa rowed once. They glided into that space. "When the front boat goes, we follow! Boats take turns too!"
Little by little, they reached the ice boat. Bung drew Ddori's hand close and held it in both hands. "Our turn!"
Bung counted while watching ahead. "One, join the back! Two, follow when the boat ahead moves! Three, hand up on my turn!" A raised hand. "One ice block, please!"
Grandpa hugged Bung's shoulder. A waited-for turn always comes. Holding the cold block, Bung called, "Boats take turns too!"
